name: security-graphql-persisted-query-policy-review
intent: Persisted GraphQL operation admission and authorization
artifacts: Persisted operation registry, hash lookup/registration, fallback full-query handling and resolver authorization.
trace: Trace who may introduce a query and whether registry admission is being mistaken for field/object authorization. Inspect alternate full-query and version paths.
experiment: In an owned schema compare an approved operation with one unregistered harmless operation and a restricted synthetic field.
disproof: Accepting arbitrary queries can be intentional; a known query hash does not grant resolver access and introspection alone proves no protected read.
repair: Enforce the declared admission policy and resolver authority independently, preserving approved client versions.
branch_decisions: Separate automatic persisted-query registration from a strict allowlist: accepting a full query on a cache miss may be normal APQ. Admission hashes do not remove resolver authorization. Verify the configured profile before treating unregistered query execution as an allowlist bypass.
operational_method: Retain the actual operation bytes, hash algorithm, computed hash, registry generation and principal permitted to register an operation. Compare a correct registry entry with a body/hash mismatch and a caller trying to replace a trusted operation ID. APQ fallback to full query may be intentional; neither a hash cache hit nor registration permission removes resolver/field authorization.
